standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the description of the finite central algebra as a matrix algebra over a finite skew field whose center is the ground field.

standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicity of a tensor product with a skew field
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that tensoring a simple algebra with a skew field whose center is the ground field stays simple.

standard_prerequisites.name: Matrix algebras and simplicity
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that a matrix algebra over a simple algebra is simple, which finishes the argument.

core_obligations: The reduction (proof lines 543-546): assuming the second algebra is the finite central one, Wedderburn's theorem writes it as a matrix algebra over a finite skew field, whose center is the ground field.

The conclusion (proof lines 547-551): tensoring the other algebra with that skew field stays simple by the cited lemma, and the tensor product with the matrix algebra is a matrix algebra over that simple algebra, hence simple.
proof_roadmap: Write the finite central algebra as a matrix algebra over a skew field.
Use that tensoring with a skew field of center the ground field preserves simplicity.
Conclude because a matrix algebra over a simple algebra is simple.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the tensor product of two simple algebras over a field is simple, provided one of them is finite and central (statement lines 537-541). The proof is a complete argument: the finite central algebra is written as a matrix algebra over a finite skew field with center the ground field by the structure theorem, which reduces the claim to tensoring the other algebra with that skew field (proof lines 543-546); the cited lemma on two-sided ideals gives simplicity there, and the description as a matrix algebra over that simple algebra gives simplicity of the tensor product (proof lines 547-551). The non-formal content is the reduction to the skew field case. The claim is H2.
